mainTopic: Whether קידוש ידים ורגלים and the כיור water are affected by לינה (staying overnight)
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation: a פסוק teaches that even services that do not hold back כפרה need קידוש ידים ורגלים. Then אילפא asks a question according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that washing is not undone overnight: does the water in the כיור become disqualified by לינה? One report says אילפא tied the water to the same dispute. רבי יצחק בר ביסנא objects. The tradition he knew from אילפא, 'the next day he does not wash from it,' was unclear, and the scholars never resolved it. The גמרא tries to prove the answer from the משנה about בן קטין's device for the כיור, but shows that this משנה can follow רבי. The bull's location in that משנה is explained by the weakness of the כהן גדול. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that washing for the pre-dawn תרומת הדשן still counts after dawn. אביי explains this according to רבי, and רבא explains it according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The amud ends as the גמרא begins an objection from a משנה in תמיד, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a service that does not hold back atonement needs washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why the פסוק is needed. Without it, we might have thought washing hands and feet is needed only for services that hold back כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that the washing of hands and feet is needed only for a service that holds back atonement, but not for a service that does not hold back atonement. So the פסוק teaches us that it is needed for both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering why a פסוק is needed. It shows the mistake we would have made without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some services, like sprinkling the blood, are needed for the כפרה to work. Others, like burning the fats on the מזבח, are not. Without the פסוק, we could have limited קידוש ידים ורגלים to the first group, so the פסוק extends it to every service.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken idea the גמרא is about to reject.
Holds back atonement: the offering does not work without it.
It teaches us. This introduces the real lesson.
A service performed in the בית המקדש.

steps.whatToRemember: קידוש ידים ורגלים is needed even for services that are not needed for the כפרה to work.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only to a service that holds back atonement,
phrases.notes: "This" means the washing of hands and feet before a service.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עֲבוֹדָה דְּלָא מְעַכְּבָא כַּפָּרָה – לָא;
phrases.english: but a service that does not hold back atonement does not need it;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to a question asked before this section (why the פסוק is needed).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the פסוק is not extra because it blocks a mistaken limitation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Washing is needed only for services that hold back כפרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing is needed for every service, including ones that do not hold back כפרה.

steps.title: Does the Basin water become disqualified overnight?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that אילפא asked a question. According to the view that washing is not affected by staying overnight, does the כיור water become disqualified overnight?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: אילפא asked a question. According to the one who says staying overnight does not affect the washing of hands and feet, what about the water of the כיור? Does it become disqualified? Maybe we say: what is this water for? For washing hands and feet. The washing itself is not ruined by staying overnight, so the water should not be either. Or maybe, since the water was made holy in a holy vessel, it does get disqualified like anything else made holy in such a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אילפא asks whether the water in the כיור becomes disqualified if it stays overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has two sides. Side one: the water is only a tool for washing, and the washing is not affected by לינה, so the water should not be affected either. Side two: the water was made holy in a כלי שרת, and things made holy in a כלי שרת become disqualified overnight.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying overnight. Many holy items become disqualified by it.
The כהן washing his hands and feet from the כיור before serving.
The Basin: the copper vessel holding the washing water.
Holy service vessels, which make their contents holy.
He asked a question.

steps.confusionAlert: Two different things are in play here. One is the washing itself: does a כהן who washed yesterday need to wash again today? The other is the water: is water left in the כיור overnight still usable? The question asks about the water, based on a view about the washing.

phrases.english: When רב דימי came,
he said that רבי יוחנן said:
אילפא asked:
According to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִינָה מוֹעֶלֶת בְּקִידּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם –
phrases.english: that staying overnight does not affect the washing of hands and feet,
what about the water of the Basin? Does it become disqualified?
Do we say: what is this water for?
For washing hands and feet,
and the washing of hands and feet itself
is not disqualified by staying overnight;
or perhaps,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דִּקְדוּשׁ לְהוּ בִּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת – מִיפַּסְלִי?
phrases.english: since the water was made holy in a service vessel, it does become disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the theme of washing hands and feet.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, does כיור water become disqualified by לינה, or does it follow the washing, which is not affected?

steps.title: אילפא answers: the water follows the same dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that אילפא answered his own question. The same dispute that exists about the washing also exists about the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי ירמיה, from רבי אמי, from רבי יוחנן: אילפא went back and answered. Just as there is a dispute about the washing, so there is a dispute about the water.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report arrives. In it, אילפא answers his question by tying the water to the washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about whether the washing is ruined overnight. אילפא says the water follows that same dispute. So רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would hold that the water is not disqualified either, which is the first side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and resolved the question.
Just as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case.

phrases.english: When רבין came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: he said that רבי ירמיה said that רבי אמי said
that רבי יוחנן said:
אילפא then went back and answered it:
just as there is a dispute about this,
phrases.notes: "This" here means the washing itself, which רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון argue about.

phrases.english: so there is a dispute about this.
phrases.notes: This second "this" means the water in the Basin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אילפא's answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The water follows the washing. Whoever says the washing is not ruined overnight also says the water is not disqualified.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא questions the report
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא is surprised by this report and challenges it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא said before him: My teacher, you say so?!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone in the room objects to the report of אילפא's answer. This sets up the next step, where he gives a different version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is not a logical argument. It challenges whether the report is accurate. He is about to quote a different tradition of what אילפא actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: You say so?! An expression of surprise that challenges a statement.
He said before him, meaning respectfully, to his teacher.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר בִּיסְנָא:
phrases.english: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא said before him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי ירמיה, and רבין is still the one reporting this.

phrases.english: My teacher, you say so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that אילפא tied the water to the dispute about washing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He questions whether the report is accurate, based on a different tradition he has heard.

steps.title: A different version: the water is good only for that night
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא quotes a different tradition from אילפא. Water in a כיור that was not sunk in the evening may be used that night, but not the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of אילפא: if they did not sink the כיור in the evening, a כהן may wash from it for the night service. The next day, he may not wash from it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of the report in step 3, he gives a different version of what אילפא said. In this version, אילפא gives a plain rule with no mention of any dispute: the כהן may wash from it at night but not the next day, and the reason is not stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, אילפא states a simple rule with no mention of any dispute. 'The next day he does not wash from it' could mean the water was ruined overnight, or only that he needs no new washing. The next step shows that the scholars could not decide between these readings.

keyTerms.meaning: They sank it: lowered the כיור into its pit so the water would not stay overnight in the vessel.
In the evening, before night.
Service done at night, such as burning parts on the מזבח.
The next day.

steps.whatToRemember: According to this version of אילפא, a כהן may wash from an unsunk כיור through the night but does not wash from it the next day. Why not is unclear, as the next step explains.
steps.whyThisMatters: This version is unclear, while the report in step 3 sounds clear. That is the basis for the objection in the next step: רבי ירמיה presents as resolved something the scholars never resolved.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what רבי אסי said
that רבי יוחנן said [in the name of אילפא]:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: a Basin that they did not sink in the evening,
phrases.notes: Sinking it into its pit kept the water from being ruined by staying overnight.

phrases.english: a כהן may wash from it for the night service,
but the next day he may not wash from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 4 by giving a different tradition of אילפא's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water in a כיור not sunk in the evening may be used for the night service, but not the next day.

steps.title: We Never Resolved This, So How Can You?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא explains his surprise. When the scholars discussed אילפא's ruling, they could not tell what 'the next day he does not wash from it' meant. Now רבי ירמיה presents it as settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: We discussed it: when אילפא said 'the next day he does not wash from it,' did he mean that he does not need to wash again? Or did he mean that the water became disqualified by staying overnight? We could not resolve it. Yet you, Master, present it as plainly resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא finishes his challenge to רבי ירמיה's statement. The scholars were unsure what אילפא meant, so רבי ירמיה cannot claim the question has a clear answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אילפא's words 'the next day he does not wash' can be read two ways. One reading: no new washing is needed, because washing is not undone overnight. The other reading: the water itself became disqualified overnight. Since nobody could decide between them, רבי יצחק בר ביסנא objects that רבי ירמיה treats the matter as decided.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we raised a question about this)
To wash (sanctify) the hands and feet
Disqualified by staying overnight
Resolved, made clear

steps.confusionAlert: 'He does not wash the next day' does NOT obviously mean the water is bad. It could just mean he does not need to wash again. That double meaning is the whole problem here.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
"The next day he does not wash [from it]" —
phrases.notes: These are אילפא's words from the previous step, about water left overnight in a כיור that was not sunk.

phrases.english: does it mean that he does not need to wash again;
or perhaps, the water became disqualified by staying overnight?
And it was not resolved for us,
yet you, Master, present it as plainly resolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יצחק בר ביסנא's challenge by showing that the tradition he quoted was ambiguous.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's statement (reported by רבין) that אילפא resolved the question of whether the כיור water is disqualified overnight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The known tradition from אילפא can be read two ways, and the scholars could not decide between them. So the matter was never actually resolved.

steps.title: Proof from בן קטין's Device for the כיור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to settle the question from a משנה. בן קטין built a device so the כיור water would not be disqualified overnight. Perhaps this משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בן קטין made twelve spigots for the כיור. He also made a device for the כיור so that its water would not become disqualified by staying overnight. What, does this not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to try to answer the open question. It suggests that the משנה, which says the water can be disqualified overnight, follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly assumes that כיור water left overnight becomes disqualified. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that washing is not undone overnight. If the משנה follows him, then even by his view the water itself is disqualified overnight, and the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול who made improvements to the כיור
Spigot, tap
A mechanism or device, here for sinking the כיור

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the main source in the סוגיא showing that כיור water can be disqualified overnight. The only question is whose view it follows.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Ben Katin made
twelve spigots for the Basin,
he also made a mechanism for the Basin
so that its water would not become disqualified by staying overnight.
What, is it not
following Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge shows the question is still open, the גמרא tries to resolve it from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That even by the view that washing is not undone overnight, the כיור water is disqualified overnight
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about בן קטין's device that kept the כיור water from becoming disqualified overnight

steps.title: No, the משנה Follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה follows רבי, not רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה about בן קטין follows רבי, so it tells us nothing about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה follows רבי, it only shows that רבי holds the water is disqualified overnight. The question about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון stays open.

phrases.english: No, it follows Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof by assigning the משנה to a different תנא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה reflects רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, but it can be read as following רבי.

steps.title: The First Part Follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, So the Later Part Should Too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. The first part of this same משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so the later part should follow him as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the first part follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the later part should also follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer that the משנה follows רבי. The earlier part of that same משנה is known to follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal assumption is that one continuous משנה follows one תנא throughout. If the opening part follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, it is hard to say the later part, about בן קטין, switches to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן –
phrases.english: But since the first part follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon —

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא נָמֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן!
phrases.english: the later part should also follow Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 8 by pointing to the earlier part of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה about בן קטין follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה is normally the view of one תנא from start to finish. The first part follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so the later part should follow him too.

steps.title: Showing the First Part Follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that the first part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The כהן גדול slaughters his bull between the אולם and the מזבח, and only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts that area as 'north.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the first part teaches: he came to his bull. The bull was standing between the אולם and the מזבח, its head to the south and its face to the west. The כהן stands on the east, facing west. Whom have you heard say that the area between the אולם and the מזבח counts as north? רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting the first part of the משנה. It shows that this part matches only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבנות of the most holy kind must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה. The משנה has the כהן גדול slaughter his bull between the אולם and the מזבח. That only works if this area counts as 'north,' which is the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance hall of the היכל
His bull (the כהן גדול's bull on יום כיפור)
North, the area where the most holy קרבנות are slaughtered
Whom have you heard who says (used to identify the author of a view)

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the first part of the בן קטין משנה seems to fit only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, because he calls the area between the אולם and the מזבח 'north.' Steps 12 to 15 will push back on this.

phrases.english: For the first part teaches:
He came to his bull;
phrases.notes: This is the כהן גדול on יום כיפור, about to slaughter his bull.

phrases.aramaic: וּפַר הָיָה עוֹמֵד בֵּין הָאוּלָם וּלְמִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: and the bull was standing between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
its head to the south and its face to the west;
and the priest stands on the east, with his face to the west.
Whom have you heard who says
that between the Entrance Hall and the altar counts as north?
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 9 by showing why the first part of the משנה must follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: That the first part of the בן קטין משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first part of the משנה, where the bull is slaughtered between the אולם and the מזבח, an area only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts as north

steps.title: A ברייתא defines how far the north area reaches
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives three growing views of 'north.' רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it runs from the מזבח's north wall to the עזרה's north wall. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רבי adds the walking areas of the כהנים and ישראל. Everyone agrees the area from the חליפות inward is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: What counts as 'north'? From the northern wall of the מזבח until the northern wall of the עזרה, and the whole stretch opposite the מזבח is north. This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רבי adds the place where the כהנים walk and the place where ישראל walk. But from the חליפות inward, everyone agrees it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its claim in step 10: a ברייתא showing that only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as 'north.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three opinions, and each one adds more area to 'north.' The area between the אולם and the מזבח first appears in רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view. That is why step 10 tied the כהן גדול's bull to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The northern part of the עזרה, where the holiest קרבנות must be slaughtered
The wall of the Temple courtyard
The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The strip where the כהנים walk
The chamber where the knives were kept

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: What counts as north?
From the northern wall of the altar
until the northern wall of the courtyard,
and the whole area opposite the entire altar is north.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon adds:
Even the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מוֹסִיף: אַף מְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: Rabbi adds: even the place where the priests walk
and the place where the Israelites walk.
But from the Chamber of the Knives and inward,
everyone agrees that it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 10's claim that only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as north.
steps.raayaObject: That the first part of the משנה (the bull between the אולם and the מזבח) follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing three expanding opinions on the boundaries of 'north'

steps.title: רבי also includes the area between the אולם and the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי builds on top of everything before him, so he also counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as north. The first part of the משנה could just as well follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that this follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and not רבי? Would רבי add to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view but not to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 10's proof. רבי's view includes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's area too, so that area does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is a ladder: each opinion keeps everything the earlier ones said and adds more. So רבי also counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as north. The bull standing there fits רבי just as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a sharp rejection)
Adds on top of an earlier view

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי adds' does not mean he adds only to the first opinion. He adds to everything listed before him, including רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's area.

phrases.english: And can you really think this?!

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא – וְלָא רַבִּי?!
phrases.english: That it follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, and not Rabbi?!

phrases.aramaic: [הַשְׁתָּא רַבִּי] אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוֹסֵיף,
phrases.english: Now, does Rabbi add onto Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording to complete the sentence.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא מוֹסֵיף?!
phrases.english: but not add onto Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn from the ברייתא in steps 10-11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the bull's location points only to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that רבי's view includes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's area as well

steps.title: Rephrasing the proof: why not the walking areas?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies its argument. It does not claim רבי excludes the area between the אולם and the מזבח. Its point is that if the משנה followed רבי, the bull could have been placed in the walking areas of the כהנים or ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we mean: if you think the משנה follows רבי, let it place the bull in the place where the כהנים walk or in the place where ישראל walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof by restating it more sharply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new argument looks at what the משנה chose. The משנה picked the area between the אולם and the מזבח. If it followed רבי, it could have named his special areas, the walking strips. Choosing this spot suggests that רבי's extra areas were not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we meant (restating an argument)
Let him stand it (the bull) there

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
If you think it follows Rabbi,
let him stand it in the place where the priests walk
phrases.notes: 'It' means the כהן גדול's bull from the משנה in step 10.

phrases.english: or in the place where the Israelites walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by recasting the proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof seemed to claim that רבי excludes the area between the אולם and the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof really asks why the משנה did not use רבי's own extra areas

steps.title: The same question hits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the argument around. If the משנה followed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the bull could stand in the basic north area, between the מזבח's north wall and the עזרה's north wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then, does it follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון? Then let it place the bull from the northern wall of the מזבח to the northern wall of the עזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument in step 13 proves too much. The same question works against רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every opinion accepts the main north area. So under any view, the משנה could have placed the bull there. The choice of the area between the אולם and the מזבח cannot reveal which opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: But what then? (turning the argument back)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאי, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא?!
phrases.english: But what then, does it follow Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?!
Then let him stand it from the northern wall of the altar
to the northern wall of the courtyard!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 13's own logic against it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'why not another valid spot?' disproves רבי, it disproves רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too, since the main north area was also available

steps.title: The bull stays close to spare the weak כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: Under any view, the bull stands between the אולם and the מזבח because the כהן גדול is weak and should not walk far. That reason works under רבי too, so the proof falls. The משנה can follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? It is because of the כהן גדול's weakness. Here too, it is because of the כהן גדול's weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason for the bull's location and ends the attempt to prove that this part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location is about convenience for a tired כהן גדול, not about which areas count as north. The same reason explains why the bull was not placed in רבי's walking areas. So the first part of the משנה does not have to follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The weakness of the כהן גדול
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The bull's spot between the אולם and the מזבח was chosen to spare the weak כהן גדול. It does not show which view of 'north' the משנה holds. So the challenge in step 9 falls, and the משנה can follow רבי, as step 8 said.
steps.whyThisMatters: This restores step 8's answer. The proof about אילפא's ruling from the בן קטין משנה is pushed aside.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
It is because of the weakness of the High Priest;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם חוּלְשָׁא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: here too, it is because of the weakness of the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles step 14's challenge with a practical reason that works for every opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects step 9's claim that the first part of the משנה must follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bull's location comes from the כהן גדול's weakness, not from the definition of north
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה can follow רבי, because the bull's location is explained by the כהן גדול's weakness.

steps.title: Washing before dawn carries over into the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a כהן who washed his hands and feet for the תרומת הדשן does not need to wash again the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If a כהן washed his hands and feet for the removal of the ashes, he does not need to wash again the next day, because he already washed at the start of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רבי יוחנן about קידוש ידים ורגלים. The washing a כהן does before dawn still works after dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומת הדשן was done before dawn, while it was still technically night. Usually a new day might seem to need a new washing. רבי יוחנן says no, because that washing was the start of this day's work.

keyTerms.meaning: The washing of hands and feet from the כיור that a כהן must do before serving
Removing ashes from the מזבח, the first service each day, done before dawn
The beginning of the day's service

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he sanctified his hands and feet for the removal of the ashes,
the next day he does not need to sanctify again,
phrases.notes: "The next day" means after dawn. The ash removal happened before dawn, which still counts as the night before.

phrases.english: since he already sanctified at the beginning of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about קידוש ידים ורגלים and whether it carries over from night to day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing done for the pre-dawn תרומת הדשן still counts after dawn, so no new washing is needed.

steps.title: Whose view does this ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רבי יוחנן follows. It does not fit רבי, who says staying overnight cancels the washing. It also does not fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the washing lasts much longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is רבי, he says that staying overnight cancels the washing. If it is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, he says you don't need to wash again even for ten days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא רבי יוחנן is following and shows that neither choice fits. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי, the night ending should cancel the washing, so the כהן should wash again. Under רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the washing lasts for days, so why speak only about tomorrow morning? רבי יוחנן's ruling is too lenient for one view and too narrow for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion is this?
Staying overnight; here, the washing being left through the night
Disqualifies, cancels

steps.confusionAlert: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is a different person from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, even though both names begin with רבי.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If according to Rabbi, doesn't he say that being left overnight disqualifies!
If according to Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
doesn't he say: he does not need to sanctify
even from now until ten days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling by showing it does not match either known view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that pre-dawn washing works after dawn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי, the overnight rule should require washing again. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the washing lasts days, so limiting it to the next morning makes no sense.

steps.title: It follows רבי, because the overnight rule is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ruling follows רבי. The overnight rule is only דרבנן, and רבי agrees it does not apply between the rooster's crow and morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It really follows רבי. The overnight rule is only rabbinic, and he agrees that from the rooster's crow until morning, staying overnight does not cancel the washing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבי. He explains why the overnight rule does not apply to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since לינה cancels the washing only by rabbinic law, the חכמים could set limits on it. Washing done from the rooster's crow onward already counts as morning washing. So the כהן who washed for the תרומת הדשן keeps his washing into the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; it is still as we first said
A rule from the חכמים, not from the תורה
The rooster's crow, before dawn
He agrees, concedes

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, it is according to Rabbi;
and the overnight disqualification is rabbinic,
and he concedes that from the rooster's crow until morning
being left overnight does not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first side of the challenge and keeps the ruling within רבי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רבי's overnight rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי, any washing before dawn is canceled when the night ends.
steps.terutzMaskana: The overnight rule is rabbinic and does not cover washing done from the rooster's crow onward.

steps.title: It follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, but only for the start of service
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ruling follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן accepted his view only for washing at the beginning of the service, not for washing at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It really follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן accepted his words for the beginning of the service, but not for the end of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same question. רבי יוחנן follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, but only in part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agreed that washing at the start of the service carries into the day. He did not agree that washing at the end of one day's service carries into the next day. That explains why he did not adopt the full "ten days" view.

keyTerms.meaning: He saw his words as correct; he agreed with him
The end of the day's service

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. According to אביי, רבי יוחנן follows רבי, because the overnight rule is rabbinic and stops at the rooster's crow. According to רבא, he follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, but only for washing at the beginning of the service.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rava said: Actually, it is Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon
[and Rabbi Yoḥanan saw his words as correct]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. They tell us רבי יוחנן agreed with him only in part.

phrases.english: at the beginning of the service, and not at the end of the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, different from אביי's, to the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial adoption of a תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יוחנן followed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, he would accept the whole ten-day rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן accepted that view only for washing at the start of the service, not at the end.

steps.title: An objection from the morning washing described in the משנה in תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from תמיד. When the other כהנים see the כהן who removed the ashes come down from the מזבח, they hurry and wash their hands and feet at the כיור. This is quoted as a source that seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection: His fellow כהנים saw that he came down from the מזבח. They ran and came over, and they hurried and washed their hands and feet from the כיור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן by quoting a משנה about the morning service. This line sets up the next move: the גמרא will soon show what this washing proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that washing for the תרומת הדשן counts for the next day's service too. Here, the משנה describes כהנים washing at the כיור right around the time of the ashes removal. The גמרא will use this scene to test whether רבי יוחנן's ruling fits the way the morning service was actually done.

keyTerms.meaning: The basin in the עזרה that the כהנים washed from
The washing of hands and feet a כהן must do before the עבודה
His fellow כהנים, the other כהנים on duty

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this line is the whole question. It only quotes the source; the גמרא explains the actual difficulty in the next lines.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
His fellow priests saw that he came down
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן who just removed the ashes from the מזבח and is coming down holding the pan.

phrases.english: and they ran and came,
they hurried and washed their hands and their feet
from the basin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי and רבא each explained whose view רבי יוחנן follows, the גמרא now challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a כהן who washed for the תרומת הדשן does not need to wash again for the next day's service
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows כהנים washing at the כיור in the morning, around the time of the ashes removal. The גמרא will argue that this washing does not fit רבי יוחנן's ruling; the exact point is spelled out in the following lines.
